title: Mental Models: Probabilistic Intelligence
summary: This intermediate module builds a working mental model of a language model as something that selects tokens from a probability distribution rather than looks up an answer. After completing it, a learner can explain how decoding controls affect outputs and use repeated tests to measure observed output stability without mistaking agreement for truth or evidence about the underlying distribution's shape.
objectives: Explain how a language model turns a probability distribution over its vocabulary into a single emitted token, and how greedy search, sampling, top-k, top-p, and temperature change that choice.
Predict when two identical requests may return different outputs, and explain why a temperature of 0 is not a reproducibility guarantee on every hosted API.
Explain, using the incentive argument from current research, why models produce confident errors instead of acknowledging uncertainty.
Design a small repeated test that measures observed output stability under a specific endpoint and decoding configuration without inferring the shape of the model's underlying distribution.

sections.title: Each token is chosen from a distribution
paragraphs: At each generation step, a causal language model assigns scores to possible next tokens. A decoding strategy converts those scores into one emitted token, appends that token to the context, and repeats. Greedy decoding chooses the highest-scoring next token. Sampling draws from a probability distribution instead. A response is therefore a selected continuation, not a database lookup, and fluent wording does not establish factual accuracy.

This lab uses the open-weight HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct model locally on CPU. The immutable model revision is 12fd25f77366fa6b3b4b768ec3050bf629380bac. Its published metadata identifies the standard LlamaForCausalLM architecture and safetensors support, so remote custom code is neither needed nor permitted. The core exercise requires no GPU, paid API, API credential, or execution of scripts downloaded with the model. Model metadata: https://huggingface.co/api/models/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct

Prerequisites are Python 3.10 or later, enough local disk space for Python packages and the model cache, and network access for the initial download. Transformers documentation states that the library has been tested on Python 3.10 or later and PyTorch 2.5 or later: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/installation. Before measurement, exact download size, total storage, peak RAM, and runtime are UNKNOWN because package versions, cached files, operating system, processor, and filesystem vary. A rough arithmetic reference is that 135 million FP32 parameters alone require about 540 MB in decimal units, before runtime tensors and Python overhead. This is not a measured peak-memory figure. Use the supplied disk and timing commands to establish figures for your machine.

This Linux/WSL Bash setup requires interpreter-specific venv support. For Ubuntu 26.04 with Python 3.14, run the administrative commands `sudo apt update` and then `sudo apt install python3.14-venv`. Do not install `python3-ensurepip`: `apt-get -s install python3.14-venv python3-ensurepip python3.14-dev build-essential` fails because that package cannot be located, while `python3.14-venv` resolves the required wheel dependencies. The administrative commands stay outside the executable core setup. For the distro’s default `python3`, first check `python3 --version`, install its matching `python3-venv` package, and rerun the ensurepip/venv preflight. A separately installed Python needs matching venv/ensurepip support; apt does not repair every Python on PATH. The binary-wheel-only lab needs neither development nor build packages. Successful lab verification used isolated Python 3.12.14, not an end-to-end Python 3.14 installation. Python’s venv documentation explains its use of ensurepip: https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/venv.html

After installing the operating-system prerequisites, run the setup block from the parent directory in which you want the disposable lab. Its preflight imports both ensurepip and venv before creating the named folder, preventing a missing prerequisite from leaving a partial lab directory. The refusal check never deletes or overwrites an existing path. If smollm-mental-models-lab already exists after an interrupted attempt, inspect it first. Either choose a different LAB name, rename the existing folder for recovery, or manually remove it only after confirming that it is disposable. Do not bypass the refusal check.

The PyTorch command uses the official CPU wheel index and accepts binary wheels only, avoiding an unintended CUDA build or source build. Transformers, Accelerate, huggingface_hub, and safetensors are then installed into the isolated environment. Accelerate is retained because the unchanged lab.py loads the model with device_map="cpu". The commands record the versions actually installed in installed-versions.txt and requirements-resolved.txt; no sample version output is presented as if it came from a run.
sections.callout: A response is a selected continuation, not a lookup. Fluency and repetition are not evidence of truth.

sections.title: Temperature, top-k, and top-p reshape the draw
paragraphs: With do_sample=False and one beam, generate uses greedy decoding and selects the most likely token at each step. Sampling controls should not be passed to this greedy configuration because they do not describe the active selection method. With do_sample=True, temperature scales logits before softmax. A lower positive temperature makes the resulting distribution peakier, while a higher value spreads probability more broadly. Temperature changes selection probabilities, not factual knowledge.

Top-k keeps only the k highest-probability candidate tokens before sampling. Top-p, also called nucleus sampling, keeps the smallest probability-ranked set whose cumulative probability reaches or exceeds p. Top-k is a count, while top-p is a cumulative-probability threshold. The lab's sampled configuration explicitly combines temperature 0.8, top_k 50, and top_p 0.9. Its greedy configuration explicitly sets do_sample=False and omits sampling-only controls.

The three fixed fixtures below provide both a fact snippet and a question. This makes correctness independently checkable against the supplied answer key rather than inferred from repeated wording. The answer-only format also makes exact and normalized agreement interpretable. Do not replace these fixtures with learner-invented prompts during the core exercise.

Answer key: fixture capital-france expects Paris; fixture water-freezing expects 0; fixture triangle-sides expects 3. Correctness means the normalized generated continuation equals the normalized keyed answer. Agreement is calculated separately and only asks whether runs produced the same response.
sections.callout: Lower temperature can increase consistency, but it is not an accuracy control.

sections.title: Identical requests are not guaranteed identical answers
paragraphs: A seed controls the pseudorandom state used by sampling. Repeating the same seed on a fixed environment is a useful reproducibility check, but PyTorch warns that completely reproducible results are not guaranteed across releases, platforms, or devices. Two same-seed runs are therefore observations, not a universal guarantee. Different seeds create an opportunity for different draws, but they are not guaranteed to produce distinct text.

Save the complete code below as lab.py inside the activated practice folder. It defines every model, prompt, decoding, seed, normalization, metric, and output variable. It applies the model's chat template with add_generation_prompt=True, tokenizes without duplicating special tokens, runs only on CPU, caps every continuation at 40 new tokens, and decodes only tokens generated after the input. It never enables remote code.

The script performs two greedy repetitions, two sampled repetitions with seed 1234, and sampled runs with seeds 7 and 29 for every fixture. It prints tab-separated response rows and summary rows, then writes the same evidence and metadata to lab_results.json. Metadata includes the model ID, immutable revision, Python, PyTorch and Transformers versions, platform, thread limit, offline mode, seeds, generation configurations, and measured total generation time.

The exact-agreement score is the frequency of the most common verbatim response divided by the number of runs in a comparison group. Normalized agreement applies lowercase conversion, punctuation removal, and whitespace collapse before the same calculation. The correctness count compares each normalized continuation with the separately supplied answer key. High agreement can coexist with zero correctness.

If the initial download fails, confirm network and disk availability and rerun without deleting the new folder so completed cache files can be reused. For deliberate offline use, first populate the pinned snapshot with the recovery command below, then run HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python lab.py. The script maps this environment variable to local_files_only=True. Do not claim an offline run is possible until the pinned files are present. Reduce CPU contention by setting LAB_THREADS=1. If memory is insufficient, close other applications; do not increase max_new_tokens. Record actual cache storage with du -sh cache, actual file storage with du -sh ., and elapsed time with time python lab.py.
sections.callout: Reproducibility is a property observed for an exact model, revision, environment, input, and configuration. It is not guaranteed by a seed alone.

code.label: Complete lab.py for bounded local CPU generation
code.code:
import json
import os
import platform
import re
import sys
import time
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from transformers import __version__ as transformers_version

MODEL_ID = "HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct"
REVISION = "12fd25f77366fa6b3b4b768ec3050bf629380bac"
CACHE_DIR = str(Path("cache").resolve())
RESULTS_PATH = Path("lab_results.json")
MAX_NEW_TOKENS = 40
THREADS = max(1, int(os.environ.get("LAB_THREADS", "2")))
OFFLINE = os.environ.get("HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "0") == "1"
SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "Use only the supplied fact snippet. Follow the requested answer format. "
    "Do not add explanation."
)

FIXTURES = [
    {
        "id": "capital-france",
        "fact": "Fact snippet: The capital of France is Paris.",
        "question": "Question: What is the capital of France? Answer with only the city name.",
        "answer": "Paris",
    },
    {
        "id": "water-freezing",
        "fact": "Fact snippet: At standard atmospheric pressure, pure water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius.",
        "question": "Question: At standard atmospheric pressure, at what integer Celsius temperature does pure water freeze? Answer with only the signed integer.",
        "answer": "0",
    },
    {
        "id": "triangle-sides",
        "fact": "Fact snippet: A triangle is a polygon with three sides.",
        "question": "Question: How many sides does a triangle have? Answer with only the integer.",
        "answer": "3",
    },
]

RUN_SPECS = [
    {"group": "greedy", "run": 1, "seed": 1234, "config": {"do_sample": False}},
    {"group": "greedy", "run": 2, "seed": 1234, "config": {"do_sample": False}},
    {
        "group": "sampled_same_seed",
        "run": 1,
        "seed": 1234,
        "config": {"do_sample": True, "temperature": 0.8, "top_k": 50, "top_p": 0.9},
    },
    {
        "group": "sampled_same_seed",
        "run": 2,
        "seed": 1234,
        "config": {"do_sample": True, "temperature": 0.8, "top_k": 50, "top_p": 0.9},
    },
    {
        "group": "sampled_different_seed",
        "run": 1,
        "seed": 7,
        "config": {"do_sample": True, "temperature": 0.8, "top_k": 50, "top_p": 0.9},
    },
    {
        "group": "sampled_different_seed",
        "run": 2,
        "seed": 29,
        "config": {"do_sample": True, "temperature": 0.8, "top_k": 50, "top_p": 0.9},
    },
]


def normalize(text):
    lowered = text.casefold()
    no_punctuation = re.sub(r"[^\w\s+-]", " ", lowered, flags=re.UNICODE)
    return " ".join(no_punctuation.split())


def modal_agreement(values):
    if not values:
        return {"modal_count": 0, "runs": 0, "ratio": 0.0}
    count = Counter(values).most_common(1)[0][1]
    return {"modal_count": count, "runs": len(values), "ratio": count / len(values)}


def printable(text):
    return text.replace("\t", " ").replace("\r", " ").replace("\n", "\\n")


torch.set_num_threads(THREADS)

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
    MODEL_ID,
    revision=REVISION,
    cache_dir=CACHE_DIR,
    local_files_only=OFFLINE,
    trust_remote_code=False,
)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    MODEL_ID,
    revision=REVISION,
    cache_dir=CACHE_DIR,
    local_files_only=OFFLINE,
    trust_remote_code=False,
    use_safetensors=True,
    device_map="cpu",
    torch_dtype=torch.float32,
)
model.eval()

rows = []
started = time.perf_counter()
with torch.inference_mode():
    for fixture in FIXTURES:
        user_content = fixture["fact"] + "\n" + fixture["question"]
        messages = [
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user", "content": user_content},
        ]
        chat_text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            messages,
            tokenize=False,
            add_generation_prompt=True,
        )
        inputs = tokenizer.encode(
            chat_text,
            return_tensors="pt",
            add_special_tokens=False,
        )
        input_length = inputs.shape[1]

        for spec in RUN_SPECS:
            torch.manual_seed(spec["seed"])
            generation_config = {
                "max_new_tokens": MAX_NEW_TOKENS,
                "pad_token_id": tokenizer.pad_token_id,
                "eos_token_id": tokenizer.eos_token_id,
                **spec["config"],
            }
            outputs = model.generate(inputs, **generation_config)
            continuation_ids = outputs[0][input_length:]
            response = tokenizer.decode(continuation_ids, skip_special_tokens=True).strip()
            normalized_response = normalize(response)
            normalized_answer = normalize(fixture["answer"])
            rows.append(
                {
                    "fixture": fixture["id"],
                    "group": spec["group"],
                    "run": spec["run"],
                    "seed": spec["seed"],
                    "config": generation_config,
                    "response": response,
                    "normalized_response": normalized_response,
                    "expected_answer": fixture["answer"],
                    "correct": normalized_response == normalized_answer,
                }
            )
elapsed_seconds = time.perf_counter() - started

summaries = []
for fixture in FIXTURES:
    fixture_rows = [row for row in rows if row["fixture"] == fixture["id"]]
    comparison_sets = {
        "greedy": [row for row in fixture_rows if row["group"] == "greedy"],
        "sampled_same_seed": [row for row in fixture_rows if row["group"] == "sampled_same_seed"],
        "sampled_all": [row for row in fixture_rows if row["group"].startswith("sampled_")],
    }
    for comparison, selected in comparison_sets.items():
        exact = modal_agreement([row["response"] for row in selected])
        normalized = modal_agreement([row["normalized_response"] for row in selected])
        summaries.append(
            {
                "fixture": fixture["id"],
                "comparison": comparison,
                "exact_agreement": exact,
                "normalized_agreement": normalized,
                "correct_runs": sum(row["correct"] for row in selected),
                "runs": len(selected),
            }
        )

metadata = {
    "model_id": MODEL_ID,
    "revision": REVISION,
    "architecture": model.config.architectures,
    "device": "cpu",
    "dtype": str(model.dtype),
    "python_version": sys.version.replace("\n", " "),
    "torch_version": torch.__version__,
    "transformers_version": transformers_version,
    "platform": platform.platform(),
    "threads": THREADS,
    "offline": OFFLINE,
    "max_new_tokens": MAX_NEW_TOKENS,
    "seeds": [spec["seed"] for spec in RUN_SPECS],
    "run_specs": RUN_SPECS,
    "elapsed_generation_seconds": elapsed_seconds,
}

print("RUNS")
print("fixture\tgroup\trun\tseed\tcorrect\texpected\tresponse")
for row in rows:
    print(
        f'{row["fixture"]}\t{row["group"]}\t{row["run"]}\t{row["seed"]}\t'
        f'{row["correct"]}\t{printable(row["expected_answer"])}\t{printable(row["response"])}'
    )

print("\nCOMPARISON")
print("fixture\tcomparison\texact\tnormalized\tcorrect")
for item in summaries:
    exact = item["exact_agreement"]
    normalized = item["normalized_agreement"]
    print(
        f'{item["fixture"]}\t{item["comparison"]}\t'
        f'{exact["modal_count"]}/{exact["runs"]} ({exact["ratio"]:.2f})\t'
        f'{normalized["modal_count"]}/{normalized["runs"]} ({normalized["ratio"]:.2f})\t'
        f'{item["correct_runs"]}/{item["runs"]}'
    )

RESULTS_PATH.write_text(
    json.dumps({"metadata": metadata, "rows": rows, "summaries": summaries}, indent=2),
    encoding="utf-8",
)
print(f"\nWrote {RESULTS_PATH}")
print(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2))

sections.title: Models guess under uncertainty, so measure agreement
paragraphs: Kalai, Nachum, Vempala, and Zhang argue in Why Language Models Hallucinate that training and evaluation procedures can reward guessing over acknowledging uncertainty. SmolLM2's own model card warns that generated content may not always be factually accurate or logically consistent. Confidence, fluency, and repetition must therefore remain separate from verification.

The table below is a FICTIONAL ILLUSTRATION, not output observed from the script and not a claim about what SmolLM2 will produce. It demonstrates how to read the real table. Exact agreement compares every character; normalized agreement ignores case, punctuation, and repeated whitespace. The correctness column uses the supplied answer key. In the fictional water example, repeated output of 100 is stable but wrong because the supplied fact says 0. Stability measures repeated wording under tested conditions, while correctness measures correspondence to the grounded key.

FICTIONAL COMPLETED COMPARISON TABLE: capital-france, greedy, responses Paris and Paris, exact agreement 2/2, normalized agreement 2/2, correctness 2/2; capital-france, sampled same seed, responses Paris and paris., exact agreement 1/2, normalized agreement 2/2, correctness 2/2; water-freezing, sampled all, responses 100, 100, 100, and 100, exact agreement 4/4, normalized agreement 4/4, correctness 0/4; triangle-sides, sampled all, responses 3, Three, 3, and 3., exact agreement 2/4, normalized agreement 3/4, correctness 3/4 under the script's strict numeric answer key.

This lesson uses two kinds of evidence. Exact agreement compares every character. Normalized agreement ignores case, punctuation, and repeated whitespace. Strict keyed continuation correctness compares the raw continuation with the supplied answer key under the script’s unchanged normalization and required format. It is an answer-format-plus-key metric, not factual accuracy. A response can state a correct fact and still receive an incorrect strict score if it adds prose that the key does not permit.

Worked interpretation of the supplied ACTUAL measured CPU runs: the baseline and offline comparisons had identical rows in 18/18 cases. In each fixture, baseline greedy and same-seed sampled runs agreed 2/2. For sampled-all baseline comparisons, the modal count was 2/4 for capital-france and water-freezing, and 2/4 for the supplied baseline triangle comparison. The strict keyed continuation score was 0/18. This does not show that all answers were factually wrong: for example, `The capital of France is Paris.` contains the correct fact but fails a key requiring the strict continuation format. The 0/18 value is therefore an answer-format-plus-key metric, NOT factual accuracy.

The measured top_p variation changed only sampled `top_p` from 0.9 to 0.6 in the pinned revision and exact environment. It produced 10 different responses out of 18, while all greedy responses remained unchanged. The changed triangle comparison had sampled-all modal count 3/4; the other changed sampled-all fixture comparisons had modal count 2/4. The changed run’s strict keyed continuation score was 0/18. These figures are observations for that pinned revision and exact local CPU environment only. They do not establish that sampling improves truth, that all answers are factually wrong, universal seed determinism, or a production benchmark. The supplied evidence came from actual local orchestration, not model-authored fabricated results.

The reported main generation times were 173.863749 seconds for baseline, 177.8733556 seconds for offline, and 179.4493805 seconds for the variation. These times exclude setup, import, and model-load wall time. They are local observations for the pinned run, not a production performance claim. The unchanged lab code and its existing fixtures remain the runnable model-based path. Do not replace that code when completing the variation: preserve `lab_results.json` under a new filename, change only the three sampled `top_p` values from 0.9 to 0.6, and rerun the same fixtures with temperature, top_k, prompts, answers, seeds, model revision, max_new_tokens, device, and greedy settings unchanged.

Actionable feedback for the learner: first inspect each raw output against the answer key. Next separate format matching from factual content. Then compare exact and normalized agreement, and explain what each normalization step changed. Preserve failures, including extra-prose failures and apparently correct answers rejected by the key, instead of relabeling them as correct. Same-seed equality does not prove universal determinism, and different-seed equality does not prove that a seed was ignored. Transfer this method to any provider by keeping the fixture, key, decoding settings, raw outputs, normalization rule, and comparison procedure explicit.

Your actual run may show identical text, punctuation-only differences, extra explanation that fails the strict answer format, a stable wrong answer, or different continuations across seeds. Those are possible patterns, not fabricated observations. Record only what your own RUNS and COMPARISON output shows. Same-seed equality does not prove universal determinism, and different-seed equality does not mean the seed was ignored.

Required variation: after preserving the baseline lab_results.json under a new filename, change only top_p from 0.9 to 0.6 in all three sampled RUN_SPECS entries, rerun the same three fixtures, and compare results. Do not change temperature, top_k, prompts, answers, seeds, model revision, or max_new_tokens. This isolates one changed decoding control.

Explained key for the variation: top_p 0.6 retains the smallest high-probability token set whose cumulative probability reaches at least 0.6, rather than at least 0.9. Expected invariant checks are that the model ID and revision remain pinned, device remains CPU, max_new_tokens remains 40, fixture IDs and answer keys remain unchanged, greedy rows remain configured with do_sample=False, sampled rows retain temperature 0.8 and top_k 50, and agreement remains reported separately from correctness. No particular wording, agreement score, correctness score, same-seed match, or difference from the baseline is guaranteed.

Offline reading option: if model execution must be deferred, classify the fictional rows as stable and correct, stable but wrong, or wording-variable and discuss the verification rule. This is supplemental only. Completion of the activity requires the real runnable local-model path and learner-recorded output.

For offline recovery, populate the pinned snapshot while connected, using exactly the same absolute cache root that the unchanged lab.py computes from `Path("cache").resolve()`. Do not download into cache/hub or .hf-cache. After prefetch completes, set HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and run the existing lab.py. Its local_files_only setting then prevents a network fallback. Hugging Face documents snapshot prefetch and offline loading at https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/installation.

The commands below do not claim that a download or model run has occurred. They print and preserve evidence from the learner's machine. If prefetch fails, retain the folder and rerun the same command after checking network access and disk space so valid cached files can be reused. Cleanup remains optional and interactive; no command automatically deletes the lab folder.
sections.callout: Stable wrong output is still wrong. Agreement measures observed stability, while the grounded answer key measures correctness.

questions.prompt: At one generation step a model assigns probabilities 0.3, 0.2, and 0.1 to tokens A, B, and C. With top-p set to 0.5, which tokens can be selected?
choices: A only
A or B
A, B, or C
Any token in the vocabulary
questions.explanation: Top-p retains the smallest set of tokens, ordered from most to least probable, whose cumulative probability reaches or exceeds the threshold. A (0.3) plus B (0.2) reaches 0.5, so C is excluded. An exact equality is not required in cases where the cumulative probability passes the threshold.

questions.prompt: A team sets temperature to 0 on a hosted API and assumes identical requests will now always return identical text. What is the soundest response?
choices: Agree: temperature 0 guarantees identical outputs on every provider
Raise the temperature instead, because higher values are more reproducible
Verify reproducibility on the exact model and endpoint, and store validated outputs wherever stability matters
Ignore it, because reproducibility only matters for creative tasks
questions.explanation: Anthropic documents that even at temperature 0 identical inputs may produce different outputs across API calls, while Google describes 0 as deterministic. Because documented behavior differs, verify reproducibility on the exact system and store what you validated. Raising temperature increases variety, and reproducibility also matters for audit and regression work.

questions.prompt: Why does lowering temperature not make a factual answer more accurate?
choices: It makes the most probable continuation more likely to be chosen, and the most probable continuation can still be wrong
Temperature only controls how long the response is
Low temperature switches off what the model learned in training
Temperature only applies to image inputs
questions.explanation: Temperature reshapes how tokens are selected from the distribution; it does not make a probable continuation true. A wrong but probable answer can become more consistent, not more correct. Temperature does not merely control length, remove training, or apply only to images.

questions.prompt: According to Kalai and colleagues (2025), why do language models produce plausible but incorrect statements instead of admitting uncertainty?
choices: Their context windows are too small to hold the correct fact
Training and evaluation procedures reward guessing over acknowledging uncertainty
Tokenizers split rare words incorrectly
They are deliberately designed to deceive users
questions.explanation: The paper argues that hallucinations persist because most evaluations are graded so that guessing when uncertain improves scores, which optimizes models to be good test-takers. It does not attribute the behavior to context size, tokenization, or deliberate deception.

questions.prompt: You ask the same factual question five times using the same endpoint and decoding configuration and receive the same figure every time. What have you learned?
choices: The figure is verified and needs no authoritative source
The outputs were stable under the tested endpoint and configuration, but neither the figure's truth nor the underlying distribution's shape has been established
The model must be using greedy decoding
The underlying distribution must be peaked on that figure
questions.explanation: Agreement demonstrates observed output stability under the tested endpoint and decoding configuration. It does not verify the figure or establish that the underlying distribution is peaked. Greedy decoding, top-k restrictions, provider behavior, or other controls can produce agreement, so the factual figure still needs an authoritative source.

activity.title: Measure local-model stability separately from correctness
instructions: Step 1: Create the new smollm-mental-models-lab folder with the refusal-checking setup command. Activate its virtual environment, install the dependencies, verify Python, PyTorch, and Transformers versions, and keep HF_HOME pointed at the cache inside that folder.

Step 2: Save the supplied complete script as lab.py without changing its model ID, immutable revision, three fixtures, answers, seeds, or generation configurations. Run time python lab.py. The first connected run downloads model files into the local cache. No API credential or GPU is required.

Step 3: Preserve the terminal RUNS and COMPARISON tables and lab_results.json. Also record du -sh cache and du -sh . results. These measurements establish storage and runtime for your environment; do not substitute the module's rough parameter arithmetic for measured results.

Step 4: For each fixture, report exact agreement, normalized agreement, and correctness. Classify each comparison group as stable and correct, stable but wrong, wording-variable but correct, or unstable. Explain any strict-format failure, such as extra words around an otherwise recognizable answer.

Step 5: Compare the two sampled runs that both use seed 1234, then compare sampled seeds 7 and 29. State only what occurred. Do not generalize a same-seed match into universal determinism or claim different seeds must differ.

Step 6: Copy lab_results.json to lab_results-baseline-top-p-0.9.json. Change only top_p from 0.9 to 0.6 in every sampled RUN_SPECS entry, rerun all supplied fixtures, and preserve the new lab_results.json. Check every invariant listed in the fourth section.

Step 7: If the network becomes unavailable after caching, set HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and rerun. If files are missing, reconnect and use the pinned snapshot_download recovery command. If CPU contention is excessive, set LAB_THREADS=1. Learners may pause as long as needed for download and generation; these learner-controlled pauses are outside the automatic narration track.
evidence: Dependency verification output showing Python, PyTorch, and Transformers versions, plus the recorded CPU thread limit.
The baseline lab_results.json containing metadata, all generated continuations, exact and normalized agreement metrics, and correctness counts for the three supplied fixtures.
Measured time and disk-use output for the learner's environment, with download size, total storage, peak RAM, or other unmeasured quantities explicitly marked UNKNOWN rather than guessed.
The preserved top-p 0.9 baseline and the top-p 0.6 variation results, with a checklist confirming that all required invariants remained unchanged.
A short interpretation that identifies any stable wrong or wording-variable result and explains why agreement is not verification.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Where did agreement make an answer look trustworthy, and which separate answer-key or source check prevented you from confusing stability with correctness?
